patch.value: Deep coverage gate exhausts its 60-minute budget on eligible local runners

GitHub issue unbraind/pm-swarm#97: the deep c8 coverage stage has a fixed 60-minute deadline that eligible local runners cannot meet at PM_TEST_TIME_SCALE=3; three deep legs on an arm64 overflow runner each died at the deadline with 825 passing tests, 39 cancelled, zero assertion failures, and one leg waited 9h30m in queue. Companion coverage item: pm-swarm-9bks.

Measure queue wait separately from execution; Use stage timings, peak memory and actual termination reasons from comparable runs before adding more CI load; Demonstrate complete deep gate receipts with time headroom for eligible runners, or document routing the heavy gate to a runner class that can finish it; Preserve existing required checks, coverage scope and thresholds, install acceptance and strict health; An incomplete run must not become a success

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Reproduction, measured from CI run 45012114155 at release head (queue wait separated from execution via the actions API): the run was created 2026-11-22T10:22:19Z. All three started deep legs ran sequentially on one Pi 4B arm64 overflow runner; each passed checkout, npm ci (about 20 s) and strict health (about 8 s), then died in the release gate step at the fixed 3600000 ms c8 deadline inside scripts/coverage-gate.ts. deep (26, bun): queued 9 h 30 m before assignment, executed 62 m 05 s. deep (22, npm): executed 63 m 13 s. deep (26, npm): executed 62 m 11 s. The interrupted receipts showed 825 passing tests, 39 cancelled, zero assertion failures in the Node 26 legs; partial coverage is not a pass and the gate correctly refused, but the deadline is a fixed constant rather than a budget sized from any measured runner runtime. The fourth leg (22, bun) was still queued over 19 h later, so queue starvation and execution budget are distinct problems. Follow-up measurements will size the c8 deadline and worker count from measured deep-leg runtime on the actual local runner classes (an x64 fleet host and a Pi 4B arm64 host, in containers capped like the controller admits them).

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Design, building the acceptance criteria: (1) scripts/coverage-gate.ts now reads the c8 wall-clock budget (coverageGate.deadlineMs) and the worker maximum (coverageGate.testConcurrency) from the manifest - both required, validated as positive integers, so the budget is a deliberate reviewed diff sized from measured deep-leg runtime instead of the hidden 3600000 constant; the worker maximum is capped by the parallelism the runner exposes (cgroup CPU quota included), verified on the runner hosts: a 2-CPU container reports 2 and a 3-CPU Pi container reports 3, so one manifest value sizes every runner class. (2) Every gate outcome that reaches its reconciliation decision emits a receipt: stage timings (configure/execute/reconcile), the actual termination reason (exit code, signal, or deadline), the worker count used, the gate process peak RSS and the remaining deadline headroom; a fully measured run also writes coverage/gate-receipt.json, which the deep workflow appends to the step summary. A refused run still invalidates every report (existing invariant kept), and no receipt ever claims complete on an incomplete run. (3) ci-deep.yml now measures queue wait separately from execution (first step fetches the run creation time from the actions API, records the runner-local execution start; an always() closing step records the execution span, the container cgroup memory.peak and the receipt), and gains read-only actions permission for the run-creation lookup; measurement steps are tolerant and can never fail the gate. (4) The job cap contract is enforced by test: the manifest deadline must leave at least 30 minutes of the 120-minute deep job for every non-coverage stage. Sizing runs with the fixed gate are executing now on an x64 fleet host and on the Pi 4B arm64 host where the deadline failures reproduced; the final deadlineMs/testConcurrency values and the eligibility/routing decision follow from those receipts.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Revert proof (behavioural revert, restored and rerun after): with only scripts/coverage-gate.ts, package.json and .github/workflows/ci-deep.yml reverted to origin/main, the new contract tests fail on clean assertions: 'the deep workflow measures queue wait separately from execution and records peak memory' (both recording steps absent), 'the manifest budget is explicit, positive and leaves the deep job headroom' (no deadlineMs in the manifest), 'a complete run writes a receipt with headroom, stage timings and its termination reason' (no receipt emitted or stored), and 'the runner receives the configured deadline and worker maximum' fails exactly on the defect: actual spawn timeout 3600000 (the hidden constant) vs expected 1234567 (the manifest budget). After restoring the fixed implementation the full file passes 9/9. Under the revert the deadline-path regression additionally stops honouring its fixture budget (a 1 ms manifest deadline waits on the hardcoded 3600000 ms constant), which is the original failure mode.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Same-defect class audit within this package: scripts/coverage-gate.ts held the only suite-runtime wall budget in the repository (the fixed 3600000 ms c8 deadline, introduced with the merge-async reporter work on pm-swarm-9bks). The other fixed child deadlines (300000 ms in scripts/changelog-pm.ts, scripts/identity-gate.ts and scripts/prepare-merge-driver.ts) govern fast single commands, not the measured test suite, and the failing deep legs show every pre-coverage release gate stage passing on the same runner class, so they are not instances of this defect. ci-deep.yml's 120-minute job cap is now derived from the same sizing contract (the manifest deadline must leave it at least half an hour). The npm and Bun release gates both execute the same coverage script through node, so both consumers inherit the sized budget and the receipt. No other fleet package's coverage gate carries a c8 spawn deadline (only this package's does), so no cross-repo instance of the defect exists yet; the queue starvation seen in the same CI run (one leg queued over 19 h, others 9.5 h) is a distinct capacity problem, tracked as a follow-up item.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Measured deep-leg runtime, x64 class (comparable run on the fleet's main x64 runner host, in a container capped exactly as the controller admits fleet jobs: 2 CPUs, 5 GiB, Node 22, PM_TEST_DEPTH=full PM_TEST_TIME_SCALE=3, 2 workers): the complete suite - 1247 tests - finished in 2480 s (41.3 min), with npm ci (warm shared cache) and build inside a 42.4-minute coverage stage wall. The gate refused because two tests need repository Git metadata that the measurement copy intentionally lacked (a fixture-repo git rev-parse and the publish-attestation verifier's tracked-repository audit); both pass in every real CI checkout and are unrelated to the coverage budget. Termination reason recorded: suite exit 1, not the deadline. So the x64 class finishes the deep coverage stage with about 19 minutes of headroom against a 3600000 ms budget - the deadline exhaustion is confined to the arm64 overflow class (the Pi 4B host reproduced it in CI at 2 workers: 825 passing, 39 cancelled at 60 minutes, roughly 2.2x slower). A second run on the same x64 host with the fixed gate, a Git checkout and the candidate shipped budget is executing to produce the complete receipt.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Measured deep-leg runtime with the fixed gate, receipts: (1) x64 fleet host, 2-CPU 5-GiB container, Node 22, scale 3, full depth, 2 workers: execute stage 2370 s (39.5 min), all 1256 tests ran, 1254 passed; the gate refused on two measurement-environment artifacts (git dubious ownership: the host-owned checkout differs from the container user; a fixture git rev-parse and the publish-attestation verifier both need repository git), with 1230 s (20.5 min) headroom against the 3600000 ms candidate budget recorded in the receipt. (2) Pi 4B arm64 host, 3-CPU 2.5-GiB container (the controller's admission caps), 3 workers, scale 3, full depth, budget raised to 2 h for measurement: execute stage 5639 s (94 min), all 1256 tests ran, 1253 passed; peak container memory about 816 MiB of 2.5 GiB (no memory pressure at 3 workers); the three failures are the same two git-ownership artifacts plus the new headroom contract test correctly refusing the measurement-only 2 h budget. (3) A contended full-depth scale-1 run on the multi-agent host reproduced the deadline mechanism live: the gate killed the run at 3600000 ms (execute stage 3719 s at kill, 1090 passed, 10 cancelled), emitted its receipt with termination kind deadline, invalidates every report and exited 1 - an incomplete run did not become a success. Sizing: the shipped budget is 1.5x the measured x64 deep-leg execute stage (39.5 min measured, 60 min budget, 50 percent headroom) with 2 workers, the measured optimum for 2-CPU containers (both runs saturated both CPUs). The Pi 4B class cannot finish even at 3 workers inside the 120-minute deep job with the required non-coverage reserve: at 2 workers CI shows 825 passing with 39 still active at 60 minutes, at 3 workers the complete stage takes 94 minutes. The arm64 overflow is therefore not an eligible runner class for this package's heavy gate; routing decision recorded in the next comment.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Routing (the acceptance alternative for the runner class that cannot finish): pm-swarm's deep legs route to the x64 runner class only. Measured: the x64 class completes the full scale-3 deep coverage stage in 39.5 min at 2 workers with 20.5 min headroom against the shipped 3600000 ms budget; the Pi 4B class needs 94 min at 3 workers (and cannot finish 2 workers inside 60 min), so no deadline that fits the 120-minute job with a non-coverage reserve can cover it. The fleet controller's repository routing config on the ops host now lists this package as x64 primary without the arm64 overflow token, so its ci-deep jobs (label pm-local) stop spilling to the Pis and queue for the x64 pool; the controller re-reads that config every cycle. The config file is host-local fleet ops state, deliberately outside this package; docs/ci-tiers.md documents the eligibility rule and the measurement. Deep legs that cannot find an admissible x64 slot queue - that is the separately tracked capacity problem (queue-starvation follow-up item), which is strictly better than occupying a Pi for 62+ minutes and failing at the deadline. Required checks, coverage scope, 100 percent thresholds, install acceptance and strict health are unchanged.
